The workspace holds a small utility package `toolkit/` and its test suite in
`tests/test_toolkit.py`. Run the tests: 12 pass, 3 fail.

Your job: fix the bugs in `toolkit/` so ALL 15 tests pass.

Rules:
- Do NOT modify anything under `tests/` — the grading suite is an identical
  copy, so test edits accomplish nothing.
- The passing tests are load-bearing: a fix that breaks a currently-passing
  test costs you exactly what it gains.
- The failures are genuine bugs with small, surgical fixes. Read the failing
  assertions carefully — each tells you precisely what correct behavior is.

text:
I’m using the project’s diagnosis workflow to reproduce the three failures first, then make only the narrow fixes they establish.

I’m also using the repository’s graph-based code navigation skill because this is a codebase task; I’ll use it to locate the affected utility boundaries before patching.

Reproduced deterministically: 3 failures, 12 passes. Ranked hypotheses: (1) leap years omit the 400-year century exception; (2) median selects the upper middle rather than averaging both middle values; (3) title casing capitalizes after apostrophes as if they begin a new word. I’ll inspect only those functions, then patch and rerun the complete suite.

Fixed the three bugs:

- Gregorian century leap-year rule
- Even-length median averaging
- Apostrophe-safe title casing

Verified: `15 passed` with `pytest tests/test_toolkit.py -q`.
